topics.title: Leaving Ravu and crossing the Changtang

concepts.learning_objective: Recall Lhamo's farewell gift and Tsetan's short cut towards Mount Kailash.
Describe the kyang, drokbas and Tibetan mastiffs seen on the plains and explain why mastiffs were prized.
Explain how Tsetan got the vehicle across the snow and ice on the pass.
Relate the author's headache and the hissing petrol tank to the effects of high altitude.
Identify how the top of the pass was marked and the custom observed there.

topics.title: The salt lake, Hor and Lake Manasarovar

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the salt-lake workcamp and the geological origin of the plateau's salt flats.
Contrast the author's bleak experience of Hor with the sanctity of Lake Manasarovar and earlier travellers' accounts.

topics.title: A troubled night and Tibetan medicine at Darchen

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the author's breathing difficulty and fear of sleeping at Darchen.
Interpret the doctor's treatment, its effect and Tsetan's parting remark.

topics.title: Waiting in Darchen and meeting Norbu

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the author was disappointed with Darchen and felt his options were limited.
Analyse why Norbu, though ill-equipped, seemed an ideal companion for the kora.

topics.title: Language, words and style of the travelogue

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret Tsetan's English and the use of interpreters in the narrative.
Infer the meanings of Tibetan words and uncommon adjectives used in the text.
Recognise how active voice shapes the style of the narrative.
Identify the lines that show the distance and lack of understanding between father and son.
Interpret the father's helplessness, the prodigal-son allusion and the longing for reconciliation.
Recall the poet and describe the stanza form and rhyme pattern of the poem.
